references.text: The preceding verse where Jesus gives the disciples the instruction to have the crowd sit down in groups of about fifty, which they now carry out in verse 15.
In Mark's parallel account of the feeding of the five thousand, Jesus commands the crowd to sit down in groups, and they sat down in groups of a hundred and fifty.
In Matthew's account of the feeding of the five thousand, Jesus orders the crowd to sit down on the grass, which corresponds to the action in Luke 9:15.
In John's account of the feeding of the five thousand, Jesus has people sit down, and there were about five thousand men. This parallels the disciples' obedience in having the crowd sit down.
At the feeding of the four thousand in Mark, Jesus commands the crowd to sit down on the ground, a similar situation where the crowd obeys and settles down for the meal.
